title: Tea Kettle
text: I was struck speechless by content so pinpoint-accurate to my current situation that it was almost frightening, I say. There was even a threat embedded in it—something to the effect of “report this here and now, and Father and the others will meet with misfortune.” I’ll say it plainly: the terrifying precision of it made my skin crawl. Just what in the world was whoever left this prophetic inscription trying to tell me!? What’s more, the light kept vanishing whenever Father or Ark glanced my way in the middle of their small talk. Were they operating it remotely somehow? With no other choice, I tracked it with my eyes, careful not to let Father or Ark notice.

What is a true godslayer, one might ask… Such a being despises eternity as a malignancy and hates it, while praising the finite nature of life. It scorns permanence and immortality, mocking eternal life and undying flesh as worthless.

Because there is an end, there is a beginning. It yearns for that which is finite, dreams daydreams to quench its thirst, and brings ruin to those who possess eternity. It is the void that has expelled everything, an anti-existence.

World creation, destruction, concept, time… no matter how much omnipotence is wielded to slaughter it, the anti-existence only grows stronger in equal or greater measure. It is an inescapable natural disaster to the immortal.

Surely it is no mystery why even the mightiest of dragons are ageless yet not deathless? It is the same reason gods who can die exist. Before this calamity, even those who cannot die will have an inescapable death—one that should not exist—carved into them. A godslayer is… a savior to the finite, and a god of death to the infinite.

On the night two days from now, when the void and chaos that is the cat announces its departure, a messenger from the heavens will intervene mid-conversation with the chaos cat—confess to it everything you are thinking. For the sake of a girl who purified her wrath, just as I did… if you wish to delay the unavoidable sorrow even by a single day, to remove the despair that awaits you, and to wish for the happiness of the heavenly messenger, then proceed. That path shall become light. It must not be allowed to remember. It must not be allowed to awaken. Souls, even when destroyed, transmigrate. But for that one, there is no such thing… those left behind cannot even hope to meet again. If you wish it… may the day that brings the same sorrow I bear come even one day later. May the dream continue without end.

In other words, since Ark and the others are going to talk about departing in two days, Fillo-tan is going to talk with Ark that very night? And at that time, I’m supposed to tell Ark what I’m thinking… that’s the gist of it, I gather. I still don’t really understand any of this, I say. Must not remember? Must not awaken? And “may it continue”… it sounds almost like a wish for something to go on despite knowing it cannot possibly be granted. …I found myself hazily recalling the time I tried to approach Ark in the middle of the night and Hou-kun called out to stop me. But I’d heard that Ark doesn’t sleep… Pondering all this, I listened to Father and the others chatting idly as the restoration work progressed.
And so, two days later.
“Hey, Ark-san!”
“Raph.”
Big Sister came marching up to Ark, looking rather cross, carrying Raph-chan in her arms.
“What’s wrong?”
“Please don’t put strange things on Raph-chan! Naofumi-sama was staring at her!”
“Raph.”
Big Sister held up Raph-chan toward Ark, showing off the tea kettle she was wearing.
“Eh? I thought it’d suit her, so I made it, but was it no good?”
“It’s not that it’s ‘no good’—Naofumi-sama had that look on his face like he liked it! If I let this slide, the sparks are going to fly right onto me, you know!”
“Dressing Raphtalia-chan up in tea kettle armor? Naofumi-kun sure knows what he’s doing—pretty advanced stuff, huh?”
“Hou-san, please don’t change the subject! He’s done this before! If word gets out that Ark-san dressed her up like this, it might just open the floodgates!”
“Well, I just thought it’d suit her, so I had her wear it.”
“Raph.”
Raph-chan puffed out her chest as if to say, well, what do you think? She really was quite the good sport about these things. Father occasionally enjoyed dressing her up in all sorts of outfits.
“Haah… why on earth have you become such a good sport about all this… Are you starting to resemble Atla-san?”
Big Sister sighed, looking somewhat despairing.
“Hmm… well, at least I didn’t have her hold an umbrella, a sake bottle, and a ledger, you know? I gave that as a present to that demon-lord-beast fellow once, and he got mad at me for it.”
“That’s a Shigaraki-ware tanuki, isn’t it! Naofumi-sama has already done that one!”
“Ah, is that so?”

“He once said something that left me with the most complicated feelings—‘Business was booming thanks to Raphtalia. Good luck charms sure are nice’—Naofumi-sama definitely had me superimposed onto that thing in his mind!”
“Sounds exactly like something Naofumi-kun would do.”

Hou-kun was laughing. So then, Ark had apparently given a similar present to someone resembling Big Sister or the Raph-species before. I had to admit, I thought it suited her too. Father really did have quite the good sense of taste, I say. Come to think of it, Father had once put loincloth-like sumo wrestler’s belts on Fillo-tan and the other Filolial-samas as well. Not just Fillo-tan—all the Filolial-samas had seemed to enjoy it thoroughly. After all, it resembled the outfits they got to wear when winning a major race in the Filolial Races.
“It’s no laughing matter!”
“Oh, let it slide that much. It’s just Naofumi-kun’s little hobby, after all.”
“But still……”
“Well, if it really bothers you that much, you’re good at illusion magic, aren’t you? Just disguise yourself.”
“If you keep nagging him too much about it, he might just secretly research and craft a tea kettle refined enough for a spirit to dwell in, you know?”
“Would that count as armor, I wonder?”
“Who knows. Spirits have their preferences too, but really, it does suit her.”
“Raph.”
Like a turtle, Raph-chan withdrew into the tea kettle. Only her face poked out, wearing a thoroughly smug expression.
“Haah… fine, I understand.”
As if realizing it was pointless to argue any further, Big Sister walked off, still carrying Raph-chan.
A little while later, Father came by the kitchen to start preparing dinner.
“Well then, I had such a good time I ended up overstaying my welcome, but I think I’ll take my leave tomorrow.”
“Sounds good. I did make this detour while taking a proper vacation myself, so I really should slow down and rest for once.”
Ark said this just as he finished his dinner.
“I see. Finally, some peace and quiet. Mostly from the bird-related direction, though.”
“Ended up being quite the troublemaker, didn’t she? That bird.”
“Eh? A cat calling someone else terrible, how rude.”
“Hou-kun isn’t the bad one here, I say! Father!”
“Well, I suppose thanks to Motoyasu, at least there wasn’t much trouble.”
“That’s certainly true. No strange nests got built, and it seems the Filolials warmed up to her as well.”
I could tell Father was indirectly saying things would finally settle down now.
“It really was quite the peaceful place. Though the scars left behind by the mastermind were pretty severe.”
“True. I’m glad we managed to get a good deal of the aftermath cleaned up, at least.”
“That part really helped me out a lot. Though I do wish someone could have kept Naofumi-sama and Spear Hero’s antics in check.”
Big Sister was still hung up on that particular point.
“Yeah, Ark-san’s cooking was amazing, just as good as my brother’s!”
At Keel’s cheerful words, Ark smiled.
“You’re welcome. If you want to eat it again, just ask Naofumi-kun.”
“Are you gonna come back again?”
“Who knows? Maybe I will, maybe I won’t. I travel all over the place, after all.”
“I see… well, I’d be happy if you came back.”
“Mm.”
Ark smiled at Keel’s response.
“And here’s a piece of advice for you, Keel-kun. Remember that crepe tree fruit you gave me? If you raise it carefully, it’ll grow even bigger. I guarantee it.”
“Really!? Woohoo! I’m gonna do it!”
Keel was as fired up as ever.
“Piyo!”

“And as for my advice for Luna-chan: among Keel-kun’s children, some will be cute, but on the flip side, some will be born strong and cool enough to make you look up in awe—so don’t get your hopes up too much either way.”
“Piyo!”
“Hey! What’s that supposed to mean!? Ark-san, just what exactly did you see about me!? Hey!?”
Fufufu, that’s a secret. Ark deflected Keel’s question with a laugh.
“Come on, Ark-san! Weren’t you supposed to be making me a medicine that turns me into a man!?”
“Sorry about that. The method I know just doesn’t seem to work in this world. There was another way, but it’s not coming to me right now.”
“Ehh! Come on, remember it! Damn it!”
Keel looked thoroughly frustrated.
